## 4. Phase 5 Status

Phase 5.1 Document Storage Foundation and Phase 5.2 Submission ↔ Document Integration are complete and runtime-accepted.

The stable design in `docs/SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_UPDATED.md` calls for:
- private Supabase Storage
- bucket `research-submissions`
- PDF-only documents
- maximum file size of 10,485,760 bytes (10 MiB)
- storage path pattern `research/{paperId}/{version}/{sanitizedFileName}`
- server-side authorization before document access
- server-generated signed URLs
- 300-second / five-minute default signed URL expiry; P.2 adds only the authorized Adviser review purpose at 1,800 seconds, with explicit local renewal offered at 1,680 seconds
- database storage of the storage path rather than a public URL

### Phase 5.2 implementation and acceptance

- Submission version calculation and eligibility checks are serialized per paper using a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock; the unique `(paper_id, version)` constraint remains the database backstop.
- If a concurrent request loses, it observes the committed state and is rejected without leaving an uploaded object.
- Adviser feedback, conditional submission status, research status, and activity log writes use one database transaction. Competing decisions cannot both commit.
- Student/Adviser notifications are attempted after the primary operation commits. Runtime fault injection confirmed notification failure does not make submission/review appear failed or roll back primary records.
- Runtime acceptance was service-level, not browser-level. Synthetic fixtures were cleaned up. Phase 5.2 required no schema or migration changes.
- Migration `0009_repository_paper_unique.sql` was not applied during Phase 5.2; it was subsequently applied only to the designated development/test database during Phase 5.4.

### Phase 5.3 — Secure Document Access — Complete

Submitted-document access requires an authenticated Student/Adviser session, positive submission ID validation, current active-account/database-role verification, Student group membership or Adviser group ownership, persisted submission/file metadata verification, and a storage path bound to the submission paper/version. Admin and Panel are denied under the submitted-document rules. Only the persisted path is passed to the existing server-only signer in private bucket `research-submissions`; no client-supplied paper, path, version, identity, role or arbitrary duration is trusted. The Phase 5.3 baseline is 300 seconds. P.2 subsequently added the fixed authorized Adviser review purpose at 1,800 seconds; Student/default downloads, repository access and publication checks remain 300 seconds. Adviser local renewal is explicit at the 1,680-second threshold.

```text
Authenticated request
→ submission ID validation
→ active-account/database-role verification
→ Student membership or Adviser ownership authorization
→ persisted submission/file metadata verification
→ storage path bound to submission paper/version
→ server-side signed URL (300-second default; authorized Adviser review purpose: 1,800 seconds)
```

All accepted live scenarios and independently verified fixture cleanup passed; see the live acceptance handoff below. No Phase 5.3 schema/migration changes were required or applied.

Already issued signed URLs may remain usable after authorization is revoked until their provider expiry (300 seconds by default; 1,800 seconds for the authorized Adviser review purpose). Local clearing/renewal does not revoke an issued capability. Legacy/nonconforming paths outside the established naming convention are intentionally rejected; do not weaken validation. Phase 5.3 full submission/review regression evidence is service-level; its browser acceptance specifically covered document access. Later P.2 evidence retains its separate scope. These are known limitations, not blockers.

Phase 5.4 — Repository Publication is complete and runtime-accepted (PASS; completion/documentation audit complete). Phase 5.5 — Repository Document Access is complete and runtime-accepted (PASS). ## 6. Stable Project Rules

These rules remain applicable:

- Layered architecture: Pages/UI → Server Actions → Zod validation → Services → Repositories → Drizzle ORM → PostgreSQL.
- Business logic and authorization belong in services.
- Repositories remain focused on data access.
- Authorization must be enforced server-side.
- Verify ownership/group access before protected operations.
- Students do not self-join research groups; advisers assign/remove students.
- A student has one active group membership.
- Preserve submission versions rather than overwriting them.
- Submission versions use unique `(paper_id, version)`.
- In-app notifications remain the operational baseline. Optional research Web Push is implemented locally but disabled and not device-accepted; activation must not change primary workflow success or existing in-app semantics.
- Notification failure must not block the primary operation.
- Panel Evaluation is excluded/deferred.
- AI assistance must not replace final human academic/review decisions.
- Supabase secret credentials remain server-only.
- Store storage paths rather than public document URLs.
- Generate signed document URLs server-side.
- Keep test and production environments/data separate.
- Never commit secrets.

### Phase 8 — New Approved Owner Decisions (2026-10-09)

The older generative AI Chatbot Guide and AI Research Summarization are
**retired**. Approved replacement:

| Audience | Feature | Provider |
|---|---|---|
| Admin (verified eligible adult) | Interpret approved non-identifying aggregate administrative report statistics | Groq API Free tier, **disabled** |

This merge records the supplied scope-change decision as documentation only. No application implementation, provider activation, manuscript editing or commit is performed.

### Security/Privacy Gate (Unresolved; Do Not Enable Groq)

- Server must verify session, active account, role, scope, and **adult
  eligibility independently**; no assumption that Admin/Adviser implies 18+.
- Trusted server-side aggregation may query authorized database metrics;
  **Groq/provider modules cannot directly** query PostgreSQL, access
  Supabase Storage, PDFs, research content, signed URLs, or arbitrary web.
- Send only approved, minimized, non-identifying aggregate statistics.
  No names, titles, abstracts, feedback text, credentials, or raw records.
- Suppress potentially identifying small-count aggregates. The numeric
  threshold and eligible metric catalog remain design decisions.
- Strict server-side request contracts, role separation, prompt-injection
  resistance, rate/concurrency limits, safe output handling, fallback and
  operational logging without sensitive payloads are mandatory.
- Provider access requires deployment egress controls where available;
  omitting model tools is not itself a network firewall.
- **Gating approvals outstanding:** Groq's applicable age/use terms,
  privacy/data processing, free-tier quota/limits and cost strategy,
  adult-verification design, deployment/security controls, and owner
  activation approval. No AI service should run before approval.
- AI must not grade, approve/reject, produce official Adviser feedback,
  or replace human research judgment.

- Architecture: one root ThemeProvider with React useSyncExternalStore, one browser preference and one reusable native ThemeSelector. Stable server snapshot renders a disabled System selector until hydration; client snapshot/subscription reads browser APIs only on the client. No theme library or added dependency. Components can be reused by a future approved Settings screen.
- Behavior: light/dark explicitly select appearance; system resolves prefers-color-scheme and tracks live browser/device changes. Missing/invalid stored preferences resolve System. Browser localStorage key thesishs-theme stores only light, dark or system when selected; no default write. Preference is per device/browser, independent of account and retained across client navigation, refresh, login pages and logout. Cross-tab storage changes synchronize selection; clearing storage returns System. Blocked storage falls back to System on page load; selection still works in memory and survives client navigation, but cannot survive a full reload without persistence.
- First paint: fixed, input-free early inline head script validates the stored preference and sets only html data-theme before visible content. Follows installed Next.js 16.2.9 preventing-flash-before-hydration guide. Root-only suppressHydrationWarning accommodates this deliberate attribute change; server content/auth rendering remains intact. Browser-native color-scheme follows effective root theme; viewport metadata allows light dark. Pre-hydration Chromium probe blocked React scripts and confirmed persisted Light wins over a Dark browser preference with the expected light body background. VM checks cover all preference/system combinations and unavailable storage. No hydration errors observed.

### Separate owner-authorized React 310 investigation - no application fix implemented

Correction to the initial failure attribution: the auth runner's accumulated error list already contained React 310 before clicking the loaded Adviser Dashboard's own Dashboard link. The dev console did emit HMR WebSocket ERR_INVALID_HTTP_RESPONSE handshake failures; this is a separate environment limitation and was not hidden as a hook exception.

Confirmed production defect: Admin -> Adviser streamed authorization redirect produces React 310 even when every POST/non-read browser request is aborted. Thus a completed notification Server Action is not necessary. GET response inspection in both dev and production found HTTP 200 with __next-page-redirect meta refresh to /dashboard for unauthorized Adviser/Student entry; Adviser fallback had already streamed. /dashboard then redirects to the account's own destination. The existing service role check is inside AdviserOverview under explicit Suspense; Student authorization is inside the route's loading boundary.

Captured production stack: updateWorkInProgressHook (minified aP) -> useMemo -> Next Router (minified L in static chunk 3t1w8zn0ilonz.js, column 217338), then React rendering frames. CDP captured the actual component/fiber ancestor stack L -> y -> h -> s -> R -> I -> F -> context/strict/root tags without props, identity or research content. The failing Router already had three current/alternate hook records and failed when requesting the subsequent memo hook. Installed source identifies L as Router in next/dist/client/components/app-router.js. React 310 decodes to 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' (https://react.dev/errors/310). No conditional application Hook call or remount defect was established in AdviserPage, DashboardShell/Navigation, NotificationProvider/Bell or ThemeProvider/Selector. The confirmed boundary is Next's root Router during a late streamed authorization redirect. Exact upstream renderer/router internals and whether a dependency patch is required remain unproven; local observation does not justify a dependency upgrade or application Hooks rewrite.

Smallest corrective proposal, NOT implemented: evaluate the Adviser role guard before returning its Suspense subtree (app/dashboard/adviser/page.tsx), retaining service-level checks. Account for the same Student loading-boundary case with an early role segment boundary (likely app/dashboard/student/layout.tsx if required). Verify redirects resolve before a protected loading subtree starts; do not weaken authorization or suppress browser errors. Avoid changing the shared notification transport merely on the discredited action-completion hypothesis. Acceptance for any approved fix: production and dev anonymous/all six cross-role redirects with zero React errors, correct-Adviser direct/refresh/self-link/Groups navigation at 360/1280, preserved loading behavior, stale/inactive-account boundaries and notification preview behavior. The proposed guard adjustment is an unvalidated candidate until separately authorized implementation and regression. Expected benefit: avoid the observed late redirect path; risk: changed streaming/loading timing and possibly redundant auth reads. No source/library/dependency fix has been made.

An automatic approval review rejected the proposed delayed-POST control because it could continue mutation-capable server actions. That command did not execute. The investigation used the safer control aborting all POST/non-read methods, which still reproduced 310. No additional mutation permission was needed or used.

## 2026-10-21 — Phase 10.1B.1 Student email verification persistence/core services

### Authority and baseline

The owner's attached Phase 10.1B.1 request explicitly authorizes backend schema definitions, migration generation/review, core verification services, development/test delivery abstraction and focused tests. It authorizes no migration application, live data writes, UI/routes, auth enforcement, real sending, installation, deployment or commit. Phase 10.1A was a source-only inspection; this handoff records implementation of the next authorized checkpoint. Read AGENTS, canonical authentication/planning handoffs, Architecture, Database, source, migrations/test patterns and installed Next.js authentication guidance. Phase 9 remains closed with documented limitations; Expo integration remains unimplemented.

### Implemented scope and exact files

- Schema: `db/schema/users.ts`, `db/schema/email-verification.ts`, `db/schema/index.ts`.
- Generated only: `db/migrations/0012_student_email_verification.sql`, `db/migrations/meta/0012_snapshot.json`, `db/migrations/meta/_journal.json`.
- Backend: `lib/repositories/email-verification.repository.ts`, `lib/services/email-verification.service.ts`, `lib/validations/email-verification.ts`, `lib/email/verification-delivery.ts`.
- Stage 1 schema compatibility: `lib/repositories/user.repository.ts`, `lib/repositories/repository-publication.repository.ts`.
- Tests: `tests/phase101b1-email-verification.unit.cjs`, `tests/phase101b1-email-verification-sql.unit.cjs`.
- Documentation: this file, `docs/SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_UPDATED.md`, `docs/DATABASE (1).md`.

Nullable timezone-aware `emailVerifiedAt` has no default/backfill. A single request row per user stores requested email, unique SHA-256 digest, expiry, optional consumed timestamp, last request time and up to five request timestamps. The timestamp array is the persisted rolling-window/count information: keep instants newer than one hour ago and reject if five remain. Requests at exactly the hour boundary age out. Primary key/FK, digest uniqueness and narrow validity checks are the only added constraints/indexes. Migration SQL is additive; no existing field/type/relationship is dropped or rewritten. It remains **UNAPPLIED**.

`requestStudentEmailVerification(delivery)` accepts no caller-selected user ID/email. It resolves the signed-in Student and locks/rechecks the current database account, including active status, role, current email and absence of verification. It generates 32 cryptographically random bytes (64 canonical hex characters), persists only SHA-256, expires in 60 minutes and applies a 60-second cooldown/five-per-rolling-hour limit. Failed and uncertain deliveries retain quota; resend after limits permit replaces the prior token, without creating another account. Already verified accounts cannot request another link.

`confirmStudentEmailVerification(token)` validates canonical token input, resolves its digest internally, then locks the same user before rereading the current token/account. Expired, consumed, superseded, changed-email, inactive, missing and non-Student states fail with controlled results. Digest/current-email/unused/expiry and active-Student conditions are rechecked on the updates. Consumption and the account verification timestamp commit together; failure throws through the transaction for rollback. Only the verification timestamp is changed on the account. Confirmation creates no normal session. There is no GET handler or automatic consumption on opening a link.

All verification writers lock the user first, consistent with Admin role/status mutation ordering; database `clock_timestamp()` is read after acquiring the lock to avoid stale transaction-start time following a wait. Token lookup outside the transaction is revalidated under the lock. Delivery occurs only after commit and outside the lock. Consequently an email can arrive after a later resend and contain a superseded link; that old link is safely rejected. There is no queue/outbox or guaranteed delivery in this scope.

Development delivery is an explicit injected callback carrying only recipient, subject and verification instructions/link. It has no default sender, SDK, real sending, routine logging or dependency addition. It rejects production/unset environments both when created and when used, and accepts only HTTP loopback page URLs without credentials/query/fragment. The mock callback captures synthetic messages in memory. A future local Mailpit adapter can use the seam; Mailpit is not installed or integrated here. Raw tokens/URLs are confined to transient server/delivery memory and are absent from service results and persistence.

### Stage 1 preservation and migration compatibility

Auth actions/services, bcrypt/JWT/cookies, registration sign-in, password login and active/role/ownership policies are unchanged. No auth path sends verification messages or requires `emailVerifiedAt`; no existing account is automatically verified/recreated and no live data/Storage is touched. Drizzle normally includes every schema column in full-row queries and even inserts with omitted values. Adding a pending column would therefore break existing operations before migration application. Narrow repository compatibility changes exclude the pending column from existing user reads and publication account reads, and use parameterized Drizzle SQL with explicit legacy columns for both public/managed inserts. Public creation reads its legacy projection within the same transaction. No client controls SQL identifiers; parameters retain column encoders/default handling. SQL-double coverage verifies these operations omit the pending column. New verification functions require the migrated schema but remain unconnected to the application.

The foundation request/confirmation business service, bcrypt/JWT/session/auth actions, schema definitions and all migration SQL/snapshots/journal are preserved. Dependency changes add Nodemailer 10.1.7 and its TypeScript definitions only, plus a local Mailpit npm script; no other locked package version was changed. SMTP needs a client and the installed stack had none; the small generic SMTP dependency avoids a custom SMTP protocol implementation. There is no provider SDK or production SMTP configuration.

### Implemented experience and security boundaries

Routes: `/dashboard/student/verify-email` displays only the current active Student's registered email and verified/unverified state, request/resend controls, actual expiry/cooldown/quota/recovery guidance and a dashboard return. Student Settings adds one Email verification link. `/verify-email` is a public confirmation shell requiring an explicit action POST; GET/rendering never consumes the token. Confirmation uses controlled success/failure copy and links to normal password login or a new request. Anonymous successful confirmation creates no session; an already-authenticated user's existing session is not replaced.

Actions ignore client-selected account/email/previous-state fields. Requests check the trusted session and current active database Student before delegating to the existing service; already-verified accounts get a controlled completed result. The existing transaction/row-lock-backed 60-second cooldown and five-per-rolling-hour policy remain authoritative, including send failures. No login/registration hook sends email and no research workflow requires verification. Admin/Adviser login and all group/history/private-storage policies are unchanged.

Exposed mutations require development mode, explicit `THESISHS_LOCAL_MAILPIT=enabled` and an exact configured HTTP loopback Origin/Host. Production refuses them even with the local flag enabled. Minimal process-local fixed-window attempt budgets: 120/minute overall, 60 request attempts/minute across sources, 10/minute per requesting account (anonymous attempts share a bucket), and 30 confirmation attempts/minute across sources. No forwarding/IP header supplies identity or a throttle key, no raw IP is retained, and the map expires/bounds entries. This is not distributed or a trustworthy per-IP limiter. Shared source budgets can temporarily deny other local callers; production mutations/sending stay disabled pending durable ingress/abuse controls.

Links now use `#token=...`, so generated tokens are absent from HTTP URLs and request logs. A small client component captures/removes the fragment and supplies a hidden form value only on explicit POST; all validation/lookup/consumption remain server-side. Same-tab hash navigation resets the form per link, including Strict Mode double effects and replacement/replayed links. Raw tokens are never visible page text or returned service data. They necessarily exist transiently in browser memory/form data and the private local inbox; no protection against a compromised browser/same-origin script or exposed inbox is claimed.

Both routes set no-referrer, noindex/nofollow/noarchive and a private/no-store policy. Production GET/POST no-store behavior is verified below. Installed Next.js hardcodes development page headers to `no-cache, must-revalidate` in base-server.js; that is the observed local limitation, not a dev no-store PASS. Confirmation GET HTML contains no token. Next.js can log Server Function arguments in development, so that logging is disabled to avoid password/token disclosure; verification-route request logging is suppressed as well. No analytics/third-party scripts were added; browser-visible font assets are local. Incorrect manually constructed query-string token URLs remain unsupported and can expose credentials to external logs; generated links use fragments.

### Local Mailpit

Mailpit v1.31.6 Windows binary was fetched from the official release, SHA-256 checked against GitHub asset metadata and installed only in ignored `node_modules/.cache/thesishs-mailpit/`; no system service, PATH/global install or administrator change. Workspace network access was needed; automatic review permitted the authorized downloads. The launcher clears inherited MP_* settings, binds SMTP 127.0.0.1:1025 and UI 127.0.0.1:8025, constrains hosts/recipients, disables relay/forwarding/webhooks/update checks/reverse DNS and blocks remote message CSS/fonts. Actual owned-process listening interfaces/ports and fresh inbox were verified. All acceptance recipients were synthetic .invalid addresses; the application adapter also refuses other recipients and production execution, has bounded SMTP timeouts and no fallback/auth/logging/file/URL access.

Setup, commands, runtime flags, installation provenance and remaining boundaries are in `docs/PHASE10_1B2_LOCAL_VERIFICATION.md`. Runtime opt-in/origin settings were supplied to owned test processes only; no environment file or secret was committed. Acceptance starts/stops only its own Mailpit and Next/Chromium processes and deletes only its run-specific inbox. The installed binary remains available for owner-run `npm.cmd run mailpit:local`.

### Implemented behavior

Active Student UI now selects a PDF, creates an intent using metadata only, directly uploads its File to private staging with progress/best-effort abort, then requires a separate Submit research click. Ready-to-submit never means academically submitted. Existing compact project selector, version history, feedback, status labels, dialog accessibility conventions and approved themes remain. Frozen metadata, own-status/renew/cancel and same-intent explicit retry/reload recovery are provided. Only the opaque locator is kept in session storage; Files, signed URLs and publishable capabilities stay in memory. Unknown results instruct status/history checks before starting anew. The obsolete public File-bearing submission action is authenticated and blocked; the old internal service remains for regression fixtures.

New server-only wiring derives the actor from the existing JWT session/current-account Student guard; the workflow rechecks locked current account/group/membership, paper scope and first-submission/latest-Revision-Required eligibility. Strict Zod metadata excludes paths, versions and actor substitution. Intent UUID/staging path are server-generated. Durable quotas are 15-minute lifetime, two live per Student, one per Student/paper and ten new per rolling hour, including rows whose capability issuance fails or which are cancelled. Per-Student account locking serializes cross-paper issuance; request UUID and frozen metadata make initiation idempotent.

Private research-submissions capability is confined to staging/submissions/<intent-id>/upload.pdf, upsert:false. Issuance reads bucket policy and requires private, PDF-only and exact 10 MiB limit, plus a modern SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY. No configuration/env file changed. The trusted provider response's exact origin/path/query and approximately two-hour expiry are validated; expiration is committed before exposure. No application JWT or privileged secret reaches the browser. An issued capability may outlive cancellation/intent expiry and is not assumed single-use or revocable.

Finalization accepts intent UUID only. The Storage adapter checks provider top-level metadata, actual response MIME/encoding/length and bounded streamed bytes, enforcing nonempty <=10,485,760 bytes and the existing %PDF- signature. Server SHA-256 and an immutable research/<paper>/vN/<intent-id>-<safe-file>.pdf plan are persisted before writing the same validated bytes without overwrite. Short prepare/commit transactions share the existing advisory namespace and consistent account/group/member/submission-before-paper/intent row locks; no Storage I/O runs while holding those transactions. Current authorization, expiry and latest version are checked again before the existing submission insert and completed-intent update commit atomically. Existing (paper_id,version) uniqueness remains.

Retries reconcile existing final bytes/digest and uncertain database acknowledgements. A completed intent returns its original submission, even after expiry, subject to current authorization. No blind final-object deletion follows errors. Best-effort Adviser notification is attempted only by a fresh acknowledged commit; completed retries do not notify. ### Deferred production security gates and expiry boundaries

The owner explicitly defers these NOT VERIFIED checks to production readiness: hosted anonymous submitted-document Server Action denial; hosted cross-group Student/Adviser document isolation; Supabase signed-upload capability path isolation; actual signed download/upload expiry enforcement; and the Storage policy review/catalog audit. Resolve them with separately approved, minimal checks before institutional rollout; a Vercel protection denial is not an application authorization result. Do not create another actor/group or mint a write capability solely to fill evidence without separate justification and approval.

Application upload intents expire after **15 minutes**. Provider signed-upload capabilities last **approximately two hours** under the documented Supabase contract; the server validates the returned expiry bound and tracks it. Such a capability may remain usable after intent expiry/cancellation; cancellation does not revoke it. Application finalization rechecks authorization, ownership, pending state and expiry before academic commit. Requested signed-download TTL is **300 seconds**. Hosted provider/edge expiry, including caching behavior, has not been proven. These are retained architectural limitations requiring production assessment, not a confirmed exploit or proof of bypass. Current final uploads request cacheControl 0; cleanup respects the latest intent/capability expiry plus its grace period.

Provider references retained from the source/evidence review: [signed-upload contract](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/file-buckets-createsigneduploadurl), [signed-download TTL](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/file-buckets-createsignedurl), and [Smart CDN expiry/cache distinction](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/cdn/smart-cdn). Documentation supports provider behavior descriptions, not verification of this deployed project; no provider request was repeated for this closure.

## Phase M.3A - shared authentication foundations and mobile JWT isolation (2026-10-29)

**Status: PASS for isolated backend foundations, with documented integration limitations.** This checkpoint implements no HTTP routes and performs no hosted, database, Storage, deployment, AI or native-client operations. ### Implemented internal contracts

- `validateCredentials(input, requiredRole?)` in `lib/services/auth.service.ts` distinguishes authenticated identity, invalid credentials, inactive/ineligible account, exhausted login budget and infrastructure failure (limiter versus credentials). Future mobile adapters must pass `ROLE_IDS.STUDENT`; existing `loginUser` remains unrestricted by mobile role and maps outcomes to the exact previous web messages. Schema ordering, password limits, legacy bcrypt handling and missing-account dummy comparison are unchanged. Ineligibility is disclosed internally only after a successful password comparison.
- `checkAuthAttempt` in `lib/services/auth-rate-limit.service.ts` returns allowed/limited/unavailable. Existing `allowAuthAttempt` remains a boolean fail-closed wrapper. Every invocation performs at most the existing single admission; login does not call both wrappers. Existing counters, operation names, HMAC format, thresholds, source trust and persistence are unchanged.
- New server-only `resolveCurrentAccount` in `lib/auth/account-principal.ts` accepts claims ONLY after the relevant signature/profile verifier. It freshly resolves the existing PostgreSQL user, requires active status and matching current role, and projects safe identity fields. Missing/deactivated/changed-role accounts are invalid; repository failure is unavailable. The cookie-facing `getCurrentAccount` wrapper retains its existing session claims/current-email result and null-on-failure behavior. It is not a client actor-ID authority.
- New server-only `lib/auth/mobile-jwt.ts` issues only whitelisted, server-derived Student identities. It uses existing jose/HS256, exact configured issuer, audience `thesishs-student-mobile`, protected header type `thesishs-mobile+jwt`, integral bounded identity/timestamps and exactly 86,400 seconds between issuance and expiry. Verification rejects other algorithms, profile/claim shapes, roles, future issuance and expired tokens, with zero clock tolerance. It returns valid/invalid/unavailable; successful cryptography does not establish current account authorization.
- Mobile configuration is lazy: missing/invalid mobile configuration does not break web startup. Existing web JWT/session/action, registration, password schema/hash, email-verification, research, database schema/repositories and dependencies were not changed.

### Configuration and operator boundary

Future server configuration requires `THESISHS_MOBILE_JWT_SECRET` (independently generated high-entropy secret, at least 32 UTF-8 bytes, no surrounding whitespace, maximum 4,096 characters, distinct from existing `JWT_SECRET`) and `THESISHS_MOBILE_JWT_ISSUER` (explicit environment-specific identifier, nonempty, maximum 255 characters, no whitespace). Existing `JWT_SECRET` must remain present. The audience/type and 24-hour lifetime are code constants, not public/mobile environment variables. No environment files or real credentials were inspected, and no real secrets were generated, rotated, persisted or configured. Test keys are synthetic in-memory values only. No environment/dependency/lockfile/Vercel setting was edited.

A future login adapter must validate Student credentials once, then issue from the returned server identity; it must not accept request-supplied user/role/expiry claims or call login admission twice. A future bearer-session adapter must verify the mobile profile, then call the fresh resolver on every request. Unavailability must remain distinguishable from invalid credentials/session without disclosing internal errors. No route, native login or external capability is enabled by this foundation.

### Session-validation throttling proposal - NOT ACTIVE

Keep login's current shared budget. A separate future mobile session-validation operation is proposed at 60 per verified account, 300 per trusted source and 1,200 global per existing 15-minute window, with a separate operation namespace. This is a design candidate requiring owner approval, not an added operation/configuration/schema/runtime policy. Do not key account budgets from unverified JWT claims; determine pre-verification global/source admission and post-verification account admission without double-counting. Existing hosted source trust still needs independent acceptance; a forwarded header alone is not proof of ingress trust.

## Phase M.3C - Student mobile authentication HTTP adapters (2026-10-29)

**Status: PASS for isolated local backend implementation only.** M.3A is committed/pushed as `080126c6608ff461cd5059ba56e63580f2c9aae3`. M.3C entered at that HEAD on feature/development with clean tree/index. The owner-approved reconciliation/amendment is the current contract authority; the earlier M.3B conversation was not available as a standalone artifact. Actual M.2 interfaces were read at Expo HEAD `8de9b150e3e89353a8fd7248b7a1e8ff27e6bdf7`, clean tree; no Expo file was changed and ordinary native authentication remains unavailable.

### Implemented HTTP contract

- `POST /api/mobile/v1/auth/login`: exactly `email` and `password` string fields in UTF-8 `application/json` (optional UTF-8 charset). A bounded stream reader admits at most 4,096 bytes, with a 10-second total body deadline; no reliance on Content-Length alone. A small flat string-object parser rejects duplicate decoded keys (including escaped aliases), unknown fields, nested values, malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8 and trailing content. It is not a general JSON parser and adds no dependency. Existing backend login schema/password behavior remains authoritative; passwords are not trimmed. Invalid bodies never enter credential checking.
- Valid login calls `validateCredentials(input, ROLE_IDS.STUDENT)` exactly once, including exactly the existing login admission. Inactive/non-Student accounts with a correct password receive generic 403; invalid credentials receive 401. Only success issues a dedicated mobile JWT. HTTP 200 is `{success:true,code:"AUTHENTICATED",message:"Login successful.",data:{user,token,expiresAt}}`.
- `GET /api/mobile/v1/session`: one Bearer credential, token at most 8,192 characters, compact JWT syntax and dedicated signature/issuer/audience/type/24-hour-profile validation. Missing/cookie-only/malformed/combined duplicate credentials and web JWTs are rejected. The application rejects duplicate values visible in Web Headers; headers discarded by an upstream HTTP ingress cannot be recovered, and raw hosted-ingress behavior is not verified here. Cookie state and client/query IDs are never authority.
- After verification and account admission, uncached account resolution requires a currently active matching Student account. Deleted, deactivated or changed-role sessions receive 401. HTTP 200 is `{success:true,code:"SESSION_VALID",message:"Session valid.",data:{user,expiresAt}}`. `expiresAt` is the original JWT exp converted to UTC ISO-8601, never renewed; no replacement token is returned.
- Both responses whitelist only `id`, `roleId`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`. No web session/cookie, redirect, internal record or group authority is issued. Backend 255-character email compatibility is retained and tested; the Expo 254/255 discrepancy is deferred to separately authorized M.3D.

Errors are fixed generic `{success:false,code,message}` without data: 400 INVALID_REQUEST; 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS/SESSION_INVALID; 403 STUDENT_ACCESS_REQUIRED; 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE; 429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED; 503 AUTH_UNAVAILABLE; 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. All handler responses carry private/no-store cache directives, nosniff, no-referrer and noindex/noarchive; session responses additionally carry `Vary: Authorization`. Signing configuration has a safe typed failure. Expected jose errors remain invalid tokens; unexpected verifier failures now propagate to generic HTTP 500 instead of being misreported as ordinary invalid sessions. No error-message string matching or raw diagnostic logging.

### Session admission and existing behavior

Separate `mobileSession` HMAC namespace, approved fixed defaults per DB-clock 900-second window: 1,200 global, 300 trusted source, 60 verified account. Global/source ingress is consumed before token verification; verified-account admission follows only successful verification and precedes current-account resolution. Each applicable bucket is consumed at most once. A separate single-account transaction reuses the existing atomic conditional upsert and clock; global/source are not consumed again. Preceding admissions remain counted on later denial. No account bucket is allocated from unverified claims.

No new table, migration, dependency or operational override is introduced. Existing limiter secret/configuration and source-trust rules are reused; arbitrary forwarded headers remain ignored. The source bucket requires the existing explicit, validated Vercel-direct mechanism. Unknown source uses global/account only. Existing development/test compatibility gating remains; production cannot disable limiting through that gate. Infrastructure failure denies admission. Existing web login/registration budgets, JWT/cookies, logout, role checks, optional verification and Phase 10 behavior remain unchanged.

### Platform contract and adaptive behavior

- `useDisplayMode()` returns `unknown`, `browser` or `standalone`. Server and initial hydration use stable `unknown` with no window/navigator read; client snapshots use the exact standalone media query or boolean iOS `navigator.standalone` fallback. Modern change events and paired legacy WebKit listeners support live updates and cleanup. Missing/partial/throwing media APIs safely retain ordinary presentation.
- `DashboardShell` exposes `data-display-mode` and renders the same links, controls and authorized children for every mode. Detection never reveals another role's content. Its existing breakpoint listener now tolerates missing media APIs and pairs legacy/modern listener cleanup.
- CSS exposes inherited `--dashboard-layout-profile` and `--dashboard-content-max-width`. Unknown/browser use profile `browser` with the unchanged 1100px maximum. Standalone defaults to compact `standalone-mobile`; >=1024px plus primary fine pointer/hover selects `standalone-desktop` with a 1280px maximum. These profile names describe presentation, not hardware identity.
- Existing responsive navigation is reused. CSS handles resize/orientation/capability changes without JS viewport tracking. Narrow desktop windows get compact presentation without touch assumptions. Only a reported coarse pointer increases standalone navigation/close target minimums to 48px; existing fine-pointer targets stay 44px. Safe-area spacing uses available inset values. Tablets/hybrid devices retain all shared navigation under their reported capabilities.
- No OS/user-agent classification, query-parameter flag, fullscreen inference or saved installation preference. Unsupported profile media queries retain a usable ordinary responsive fallback. No redesign, bottom navigation, new screen, placeholder research record, branding/theme change or new interactive control.

Supported navigation is blocked while feedback is being submitted, with synchronous duplicate-submit protection. Failures retain input; success clears the draft and refreshes the existing route. **Limit:** same-document browser Back/Forward, arbitrary programmatic router navigation and mobile process termination cannot be universally blocked by this App Router boundary. The visible dirty notice directs users to the guarded page links/version selector. No history monkey-patching or browser-storage draft recovery is introduced.
- Start Review retains existing ownership/current-account checks and adds `status = Submitted` to the SQL update by ID. Zero affected rows return a safe refresh/conflict response. This prevents stale/repeated starts from overwriting Under Review, Approved or Revision Required. No feedback/activity/notification semantics were redesigned. Atomic ownership revalidation during concurrent group reassignment remains deferred for explicit security review.

## Phase 10.P2B.1 PDF access runtime hotfix (2026-10-31)

**Status: focused hotfix validation PASS; owner browser/Desktop PWA retest pending. P.2C is not accepted and P.2B is not closed.** The owner reported `TypeError: Illegal invocation` while opening the PDF separately, with Requesting state and a stranded preparation tab. This is owner-observed workspace evidence, distinct from earlier diagnostic compatibility checks and automated tests.

Preflight and final Git baseline: `feature/development`, HEAD `6f2d350cfec4dd1ac2735a13f1a01533082d0ec7`, empty index, 17 pending P.2B paths preserved. Only six of those paths were edited for this hotfix:

**Confirmed cause and minimal correction:** The controller stored native `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` references and invoked them as controller methods, giving them the wrong receiver. Initial scheduling also occurred before the request's `try`, allowing rejection to escape and leaving Requesting state behind. Before implementation changes, two new regressions failed with Illegal invocation: a receiver-sensitive browser-global simulation and a throwing scheduler. Existing arrow-function timer doubles and the synthetic UI's fake clock had missed this native receiver requirement.

Default timers now call `globalThis.setTimeout`/`globalThis.clearTimeout` through wrappers; `now` calls `Date.now()` through a wrapper. Initialization is inside the request error boundary. One guarded timer covers pending and available states against the unchanged 240,000ms deadline measured from request start; success no longer replaces it with a duplicate schedule. Cancellation cannot abort cleanup, and active/generation guards make cancelled, stale and disposed callbacks inert. Signing failure produces an unavailable state and permits explicit retry; no signing action, authorization or provider lifetime changed.

Separate opening remains synchronous with the click, removes the opener and sets no-referrer before navigation. Prepared-tab setup, authorization and navigation are covered by `try/catch/finally`. Failed authorization/timer initialization closes only that still-blank placeholder and shows recoverable guidance; disposal closes a pending placeholder. A user-navigated or successfully opened document tab is retained. Popup blocking is detected even when an existing valid URL is reused. The main page never navigates as a fallback, preserving its existing unsaved-feedback protection. Signed URLs remain in memory and are neither logged nor persisted.

**Executed evidence:**

- Extended P.2B unit suite **11/11 PASS**, including the two initially failing regressions, repeated requests with one timer, stale cancelled callbacks, cancellation failure, disposal during pending signing, expiry/renewal and existing authorization tests.
- Existing Adviser regression script PASS; P.1 detector/shell suite **7/7 PASS**, recorded separately rather than as new unique coverage.
- Focused synthetic UI PASS in one isolated headless Chromium context using sequential native-clock and fake-clock pages, with intercepted in-memory responses only. Covers real browser timer invocation and separate opening, reused access, signing denial/exception, timer initialization failure, popup blocking and pending-request disposal, plus retained workspace/draft/expiry checks. Zero page/console errors and no unexpected requests. An initial run stopped at an iframe-message assertion after replacing the clock on an already initialized React page; initializing each page with one consistent clock resolved that harness failure. The synthetic document response is HTML, so this does not establish actual native PDF rendering.
- TypeScript (`--noEmit --incremental false`), targeted ESLint and `git diff --check` PASS. ### Approved implementation decisions

- Retain the 58/42 split, 1720px route-only cap, 1080px container threshold and tall native iframe. On supported wide standalone desktops, CSS subgrid shares heading, toolbar/status and working-content rows across panels. The reading surface and review body start together without fixed offsets. Only the review body scrolls within the wide panel; no sticky overlay.
- PDF access uses compact icon-and-label semantic buttons, 36px minimum height for fine-pointer desktop and 44px otherwise, with inherited focus treatment and truthful access status in the wrapping toolbar. Loading/expiry/error messages remain accessible. Viewer-event guidance moves below the frame so it does not separate the toolbar from reading. Icons are small inline line drawings with hidden decorative SVGs; no icon dependency, tooltip, animation or new navigation. PDF authorization, generation/disposal protections, four-minute deadline and popup fallback are unchanged.
- Manrope is the owner-approved principal font. The root uses the existing `next/font/google` architecture with a single variable `Manrope`, Latin preload, `display: swap` and Arial/Helvetica/sans-serif fallbacks. `--font-manrope` feeds shared `--font-app` and Tailwind sans tokens. Body and native form controls inherit this family; button weights remain defined by existing styles. Unused Geist loaders are removed; the monospace token uses system monospace fallbacks. A source audit found no competing role/auth/dashboard font-family overrides outside the shared font setup. No font package, checked-in binary or unrelated asset.
- Full official [Manrope OFL notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/manrope/OFL.txt) is preserved byte-for-byte in `public/licenses/manrope-OFL.txt` and served at `/licenses/manrope-OFL.txt`; SHA-256 `58172e0c0fac2cda8a37b348164bb55e44b0e69051e557e92b1d3f6910141f7b`. The [Google Fonts metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/manrope/METADATA.pb) records its variable 200-800 weight range. Native document/viewer fonts are excluded. DESIGN.md records the newly approved typography decision; this is not a theme overhaul.
- Valid feedback starts an inline three-second confirmation naming the decision and immutable submission ID. Native constraints and nonblank comments run first. The exact ID/comments/decision are frozen in memory. Inputs stay editable during countdown; either input change invalidates confirmation. Cancel is neutral, keyboard-focused on entry and available until dispatch; it preserves the draft and returns focus to Submit. Per-second countdown text is not an aria-live stream; one status announcement explains the decision and cancellation window. Existing blue Submit remains primary.
- `startReviewCountdown` uses a request-start deadline, wrapped global timer calls, explicit cancellation and an active guard. No Server Action is invoked before expiry. A synchronous busy guard and attempt generation prevent duplicate countdowns/requests; the callback consumes the frozen payload once. Cancel, unmount, Activity hide and attempted guarded navigation/unload cancel confirmation. `ReviewDraftBoundary` registers the form's cancel callback so it is invalidated before a potentially blocking leave prompt or router push, rather than waiting for unmount.
- At dispatch, Cancel disappears, fields/Submit lock, status says the sent request cannot be canceled, and existing pending-navigation protection remains. Only an actual successful action response clears the draft and refreshes read-only content. Failure/exception retains input and permits a new confirmation. Late responses after disposal/version change cannot refresh or update a new submission. If an already-sent request's component is hidden/disposed and restored, it stays locked with an outcome-unknown reload message; cancellation of sent work is never promised. A refresh error after confirmed save keeps the form locked and asks for reload instead of offering another decision.
- Server Action, Zod schema, service transaction/authorization, decision semantics and conditional Start Review SQL are unchanged. This is a client-side pre-submission delay, not an undo mechanism or server idempotency replacement. Existing browser-history/programmatic/mobile-termination draft limits remain documented; timer cleanup occurs on actual component disposal.

### Interaction and layout

- Editing comments/decision does not mutate. **Review & Confirm Decision** runs native/nonblank client validation and captures a frozen independent copy of the exact submission ID, decision and full comments. The inline confirmation displays the actual decision, submission ID and a clearly labeled feedback summary of up to 240 characters. The full captured feedback is retained for submission; nothing is logged/persisted.
- **Back to Edit** closes confirmation and preserves both original inputs, returning focus to the review trigger. Inputs remain editable while confirmation is open; any edit closes/invalidate it. Guarded navigation/unload, version change, unmount and Activity hide invalidate the current confirmation. No interval, timeout, deadline, hold interaction or automatic review submission exists.
- **Confirm & Submit** explicitly rechecks the snapshot against the current draft, consumes it synchronously, and invokes the existing action once. A synchronous in-flight guard prevents double activation. Pending fields/buttons lock and status makes clear that a sent request cannot be canceled. Failure/exception preserves the draft for another explicit review/confirm attempt; success clears/refreshes only after the server reports success. Attempt/disposal checks and the conservative restored-request unknown-outcome state remain intact.
- The former review timer utility is replaced by pure snapshot creation/matching functions. Countdown state, labels, callbacks and four obsolete countdown unit cases are removed. The separate PDF-access timer implementation and its native-receiver/expiry/renewal regressions are untouched.
- **Assessment Criteria** is a compact informational section after current review controls, preserving the accepted PDF/form alignment and prominence of feedback/decision. It truthfully states that criteria-based assessment is planned and unavailable, and that current general feedback/decision can be used. There are no interactive controls, scores, mandatory criteria, fake completed work or evaluation values. The section is omitted for completed read-only reviews. No schema, criteria service, validation rule or additional action.
- The accepted 58/42 layout, route width, shared alignment rows, tall iframe, compact PDF toolbar, Manrope, themes, keyboard focus and PDF signing/lifecycle are preserved. ### Compatibility audit and decision

- `db/schema/feedback.ts`: `feedbacks.comments` is non-null PostgreSQL `text`, not varchar. There is no schema length constraint or formatting discriminator. The action/service/repository and Student workspace DTO carry strings. The existing action Zod rule trimmed and required comments and limited them to 5,000 JavaScript UTF-16 code units; the service previously enforced only nonblank comments. Both now use the same strict format/visible-text validation.
- Write path: `createAdviserFeedbackAction` -> `createFeedbackSchema` -> `createAdviserFeedback` -> `persistAdviserDecision` atomic transaction. Generic `createFeedback` is a retained low-level repository helper, not a new formatting endpoint. Existing transaction/status/account/ownership/activity semantics remain unchanged.
- Readers: Adviser detail recorded feedback, Student `StudentResearch` version history and Student dashboard latest-feedback excerpt. Shared `FeedbackContent` now adapts all three and confirmation. `student-feedback.service`, `student-workspace.service`, feedback repository and Adviser details projection preserve encoded strings without reinterpretation. Notifications/activity descriptions contain decision/version/title metadata, not comments. No Admin/repository/export/logging feedback-body consumer was found; no arbitrary representation is sent to those surfaces. Future text-only consumers must call `feedbackPlainText`.
- Selected migration-free representation: literal legacy strings and an explicit reserved `\u001eTHESISHS_FEEDBACK:1\n` prefix with strict JSON `{version:1,blocks:[...]}` for formatted content. Blocks are flat paragraphs, bulleted lists or numbered lists; inline runs contain text and optional boolean bold/italic/underline. Plain new paragraphs may stay plain strings. Markdown/HTML-like historical text and unmarked JSON remain literal. No data rewrite, arbitrary HTML, new API shape or dependency. The explicit namespace avoids guessing old Markdown symbols; malformed known-version reads show a safe unavailable notice. Unknown/invalid encoded writes are rejected.
- Bounds: meaningful extracted text must be nonblank, maximum **5,000 trimmed UTF-16 units**, counting line breaks between blocks/items but excluding JSON overhead; encoded maximum 524,288 units, 256 blocks/items per list, 10,000 runs. Unknown attributes, links, images, scripts, unsupported nodes and nested blocks are rejected by the server schema. User-entered HTML-looking text is allowed only as escaped text. Trimming literal input cannot promote it into an unvalidated encoded record.
- Research basis: project patterns and installed Next.js client-boundary guide first, then [MDN execCommand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/execCommand), [inputType](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/InputEvent/inputType) and [beforeinput](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/beforeinput_event). Native editing commands are deprecated but preserve the undo buffer, with no equivalent simple direct-DOM replacement. The adapter is isolated and tested on Chromium; future browser removal requires reassessment. No unapproved editor dependency, Markdown parser or HTML sanitizer was introduced.

`ReviewDraftBoundary` now publishes a separate dirty/session status context while retaining the original stable guard-control object and its synchronous ref updates. Clean state/success removes the indicator; failures and Back to Edit retain it. There is no automatic saving.

The title is `Unsaved feedback`; explanation is `Leaving this review may discard your changes.` Active display time is **7000ms**, unchanged by keystrokes. The upstream pause behavior is retained for focus, pointer interaction and hidden documents; hover alone does not pause this integration. The visual enters upward in 350ms and leaves downward in approximately 245ms (or a restrained 300ms down-swipe), followed by source phase/collapse cleanup. Close and Escape are optional alternatives to waiting/swiping. Safe receiver-preserving browser timers control expiration independently of the cosmetic Web Animation fuse; cleanup cancels timers, frame callbacks, Web Animations, Motion values and placement observers/listeners, with active guards against delayed completions after disposal. No uncontrolled retries/polling or global toast migration.

A body portal escapes the review container's containing block. Placement prefers the bottom-right unobstructed viewport position with safe-area/visual-viewport accounting, then searches nearby free space while avoiding the PDF, editor, links, formatting/review controls and confirmation region. Scroll/resize/focus and relevant element resizing trigger coalesced measurement. If a small/zoomed viewport has no safe floating slot, a compact reserved in-flow position beside the indicator takes precedence over covering controls; that fallback can require scrolling to the feedback area. The same toast instance/timer survives repositioning. No new application scroll container or PDF scrollbar change.

Shared neutral surface/foreground/blue fuse and Manrope tokens respect Light/Dark/System. Close targets are 36px desktop and 44px touch. Focus rings, forced-colors borders/text and live reduced-motion subscription are retained; reduced motion suppresses translation and the animated fuse. One persistent polite live region updates on dirty state, not keystrokes; the visual toast suppresses duplicate live announcements. Appearance and timeout preserve keyboard focus; automatic expiry pauses while focus is inside the toast. Explicit dismissal can return to the editor without scrolling, unless the user has already focused another control. The compact indicator and nonvisual guard limitations remain after expiry. No focus trap or modal behavior.

## Phase 10.P3C.1 push subscription backend foundation (2026-11-01)

**Implemented locally, disabled and not operational; migration prepared NOT APPLIED.** Entry baseline: `feature/development`, `b4352d1ea456dfce18097b039f9237ef46fc33a6`, clean tree/index. P.2 is owner accepted and locally closed in that commit; P.1 remains closed. The owner separately authorized this backend implementation. No closure/commit of P.3 is implied.

### Local contracts

- `/api/push/subscription`: GET returns `{ok:true,available,publicKey,keyId,enrollment}`; POST accepts `{expectedGeneration:UUID|null,registrationId:UUID,subscription:{endpoint,expirationTime:number|null,keys:{p256dh,auth}}}`; DELETE accepts `{generations:[UUID]}` with one or two distinct locally known current/pending IDs. Mutation successes return `{ok:true,enrollment}`. Enrollment includes generation, enabled, endpoint SHA-256 fingerprint, authorization expiry and key ID only. Raw endpoint and encryption keys never leave the repository. Identical registration-ID/material retries return the existing result without extending authorization. New attempts must use fresh UUIDs.
- Existing verified cookie session plus uncached active-account/role resolution; Student/Adviser only. Repository user-row locks serialize first enrollment/replacement/removal and repeat active role/session-expiry checks. Unique user/endpoint/UUID constraints enforce isolation. Expected-generation conflicts and endpoint/ID collisions share a generic 409. Conditional cleanup leaves newer registrations intact. Removal inserts a disabled generation barrier even when a pending first POST has not committed, and clears all capability fields. The backend supports later lifecycle cleanup; no logout/account-switch UI integration was added here.
- Mutations require the exact server-configured `THESISHS_PUSH_ORIGIN`, reject missing/null/foreign Origin and cross-site Fetch Metadata, require JSON and enforce 4,096 bytes while reading the stream. Strict Zod fields, canonical base64url keys, valid uncompressed P-256 point, coherent future browser expiration and bounded canonical HTTPS endpoints are required. Provider policy permits exact `fcm.googleapis.com` and valid subdomains of `push.apple.com`; credentials, fragments, nonstandard ports, IP/private/other hosts and malformed host syntax are rejected. No provider request is made; DNS rebinding, redirect/TLS transport enforcement remains P.3D work.
- Shared 15-minute limiter operations: `pushMutation` 20/account, 120/trusted-source, 600/global; `pushStatus` 60/account, 300/source, 1,200/global. Ingress consumes global/source once; verified authorized accounts alone consume account buckets once. No client-selected account bucket, new table, external limiter or change to existing login/mobile thresholds. Existing explicit Development/test limiter gate is retained; hosted/production limiting fails closed. Errors use `{ok:false,code,message}` with safe 400/401/403/409/413/415/429/503 outcomes; 429 includes Retry-After 900. Responses are no-store with nosniff and no permissive CORS or raw error logging.
- Configuration defaults to `THESISHS_WEB_PUSH_ENABLED=false`. Enabling would require exact `true`, trusted Origin, valid public `THESISHS_WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY` and bounded `THESISHS_WEB_PUSH_KEY_ID`; none was configured. No private key setting or key generation was introduced. Public configuration is returned only when available. DELETE does not require enrollment enabled/public key, but still requires trusted Origin/authentication. GET/DELETE require the prepared table; before approved migration application they fail safely with 503 if persistence is unavailable. Existing application functionality is independent.

Missing/malformed/unexpected data displays the fixed generic notification and dashboard fallback. Title is ThesiSHS AI; body is "A research update is available. Open ThesiSHS AI to view it." No private names/IDs/research/document URLs or arbitrary notification text/URLs. Clicking closes the notification and focuses an existing app window; a recognized same-origin worker message invokes a controlled application intent. - Enable preloads worker readiness and GET configuration; no automatic permission call. The explicit click calls native PushManager.subscribe with userVisibleOnly/applicationServerKey before awaiting unrelated work, allowing the browser permission flow. Already granted permission alone is not enrollment. Reuse requires a recognized same-account browser subscription/key. Unknown/old subscriptions are cleared first and require another Enable click. POST uses exactly P.3C.1 fields and updates enrollment only after server success. An uncertain POST is reconciled or conditionally disabled before another attempt, preventing accumulating unknown pending generations. DELETE carries only captured bound/pending generations, with server CAS protections retained. Native unsubscribe additionally compares captured endpoint and encryption keys to avoid revoking a replacement even if an endpoint is reused.
- Narrow necessary contract addition: browser GET/POST/DELETE sends optional `X-ThesiSHS-Push-Account` expected context. The service compares it with the already verified session user before account admission/mutation; mismatch is a safe 401. This is not a new authentication system, authoritative client ID or JSON field. Existing clients without the header retain P.3C.1 behavior. Browser requests are same-origin/no-store, reject redirects, have a three-second abort deadline and never log endpoints/keys.
- Cancellation epochs prevent stale/native/API responses from updating a disposed/new context. Verified session expiry aborts work and disables enrollment controls. Foreground status refresh never prompts or automatically renews. Logout cleanup runs only after the existing capture-phase draft guard allows the Logout click. It aborts pending enrollment, conditionally removes captured IDs and safely unsubscribes the captured native capability. Infrastructure cleanup failure attempts known native revocation; authentication mismatch does not trigger that fallback. A one-second deadline aborts API work/disposes callbacks, then the unchanged logout action deletes the cookie regardless of cleanup outcome. No broad auth/review action refactor.
- Default-disabled/unconfigured clients do not create a worker, request permission, subscribe, deliver or automatically call the subscription API. Reading an existing owned browser registration permits explicit local cleanup. No actual VAPID values were configured. Native PushManager storage is the platform facility; application code adds no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cache persistence of subscription material or private research.

### Scheduling, budget and cleanup limitations

Both invoking pages now explicitly declare Node/60 seconds (Student setting retained; Adviser detail declaration added without UI changes). A monotonic clock starts at action entry, with a conservative 55-second cutoff, five-second overhead reserve and >=4 seconds required both when scheduling and when `after()` executes. One attempt targets three seconds for lazy import, lookup, validation/signing, transport and cleanup. HTTP abort destroys the underlying request, including during DNS/TLS setup; 1.2-second socket inactivity is an additional bound, not the complete deadline. Database transactions request 250ms lock/750ms statement limits, checking expiry between phases and before later network/cleanup work.

**No absolute three-second guarantee:** the guarded adapter does not expose query.cancel(), so pool acquisition, existing five-second connection timeout, hosted identity queries before local timeout settings, transaction acknowledgement and event-loop delay can overrun the target. Every database promise is awaited; no Promise.race abandonment, shared-pool closure or new connection bypass. OS getaddrinfo cannot itself be forcibly cancelled, but expired results cannot initiate a socket. `after()` is supported by installed Next.js 16.3.8 Server Functions and documented Vercel integration, but adds no execution time/durability. The cutoff is an action-entry estimate with reserve, not an observed provider deadline. Real hosted timing remains unverified.

Lookup joins current users to enabled, unexpired subscriptions by exact authorized role/recipient and current key ID. Provider 404/410 disables only captured user/generation/endpoint, rotates the disabled barrier and erases all capability fields. A replacement survives stale cleanup. Other failures retain the subscription, with no retries. Provider TTL is 300 seconds/normal urgency. Acceptance is not display/read confirmation; process termination, deadline exhaustion, uncertain commits and device/OS conditions can lose notifications. Already queued/displayed notifications and revocation after a lookup cannot be universally recalled. Existing shared-device, cookie, reassignment and deferred hosted-security limitations remain.

### Root cause and exact correction

`ResearchPushClient.present()` checked native permission, local/server fingerprint binding, enabled state, generation, lease and public-key compatibility, but omitted the VAPID key-ID comparison. An unchanged public key with persisted `key-v1` and configured `key-v2` therefore displayed enabled while the sender's correct current-key-ID SQL filter excluded the enrollment.

The production change is one additional condition: `this.status.enrollment.vapidKeyId === this.status.keyId`. The existing safe GET DTO already provides both identifiers; no API, persistence or sender adjustment is needed. A mismatch now presents the existing ready state and explicit Enable Notifications action. No new subscription data or private material is exposed.

No automatic renewal, replacement, permission request or unsubscribe occurs on refresh. For an unchanged compatible public key, an explicit Enable reuses the browser subscription and sends a fresh registration ID with the captured expected generation, recording the current server key ID. If the browser key is incompatible, the existing first-click cleanup validates the captured local subscription; a second explicit click creates the compatible native subscription before generation-safe registration. Existing foreign-account preparation, conditional deletion, stale callbacks, one-active-device policy and denied/unavailable/unsupported states remain unchanged.

### Implemented behavior

Both tables are project-scoped, use serial PKs and integer restrictive paper/user FKs, timezone-aware creation/update timestamps, named text/status/version CHECKs and only the proposed indexes. Tasks support nullable assignee/description/calendar due date and exactly `To Do`, `In Progress`, `Done`. Notes hold required plain text, optional task association, integer version and nullable deletion timestamp. `UNIQUE group_tasks(id,paper_id)` plus restrictive composite note/task FK enforces same-paper association. Schema source is intentionally ahead of migration history; see [exact types and SQL requirements](DATABASE%20%281%29.md#c2-collaborative-research-workspace-schema-source-2026-11-05).

All 13 backend operations independently validate strict Zod inputs and session-derived identity, then use one transaction-scoped Student authorization helper. It returns `{studentId,groupId,paperId}` only after current active account/Student role, membership, active group and paper/group checks. No action accepts actor/group/creator authority. The helper composes the existing JWT session and relational model rather than creating new memberships or trusting `getStudentResearch` as a complete guard.

Write lock order is involved accounts sorted by ID, group, relevant membership rows, rechecked paper, then task and note writes. Accounts use FOR UPDATE for mutations, including creator and proposed assignee where applicable; scope rows use FOR SHARE. A changed paper group or task creator hint denies the operation. Existing memberships are protected against removal. The creator account lock is also intended to serialize the existing users-FK check for membership insertion against an absent-membership orphan decision. Reads use shared scope locks and reauthorize each request. No provider/network operation or academic submission advisory lock is introduced. Real lock behavior and privileges remain pending acceptance.

Task create/list/details edit/assignment/status/delete are implemented. Any current authorized member can create/read; only the eligible creator edits details/deletes; creator or eligible assignee changes status. Assignment targets must be active Student members of the same group. **Final owner orphan decision is implemented:** any current authorized member can reassign/unassign only if the original creator has left, become inactive or changed role. This recovery grants no details-edit/delete/status permission by itself and stores no orphan flag. Removed assignee IDs remain recorded; those users cannot mutate while ineligible.

Task deletion locks the task, unlinks all linked notes including deleted notes, increments note versions and timestamps, then deletes the task in one transaction. Errors or a missing delete result throw so partial unlinking cannot be committed. Task linking takes a SHARE lock before touching the note, conflicting with deletion's UPDATE lock. Content, creator, note identity and deletion state survive task deletion.

Notes implement create/list/view/edit/link/unlink/soft deletion/restoration. Any authorized current member reads visible notes; only their eligible creator edits, links, deletes or restores. A task creator has no authority over someone else's note content. Normal listings omit deleted notes. Explicit `deletedOnly:true` is creator-filtered, and an individually requested deleted note is visible only to its eligible creator. There is no permanent purge.

Every note mutation requires an expected version. UPDATE predicates include note ID, authorized paper, creator, version and correct deletion state; version increments and timestamps are SQL expressions in the same UPDATE/RETURNING. Zero rows triggers a scoped lookup: missing/foreign-owned/wrong-state rows return safe unavailable, while a verified mismatching version returns conflict. Edit/link/delete/restore and task-driven unlinking all advance versions. Conflict results let a later C4 interface preserve unsaved text; no auto-overwrite/merge or persistent client draft store exists.

Results distinguish success, validation, unavailable/unauthorized, conflict and infrastructure failure with safe messages. Driver/commit uncertainty says reload/verify before retrying. Successful actions invalidate only the future `/dashboard/student/workspace` route. If revalidation fails after saving, the saved success remains explicit with `refreshRequired:true`.

Executed only offline generation: `npx.cmd --no-install drizzle-kit generate --name=collaborative_research_workspace`. Drizzle generated the SQL/snapshot/journal; none was manually invented or rewritten. The generated SQL was inspected before tooling changes. No existing table/schema object changes, data rewrites, DROP/TRUNCATE, cascading deletion or grants were proposed.

`group_tasks` has ten columns: serial PK; required paper/creator IDs; bounded nonblank title; nullable bounded description, assignee and date; default `To Do` with the exact three-status CHECK; timezone-aware creation/update defaults. It includes the approved `(id,paper_id)` UNIQUE and `(paper_id,created_at,id)` index. `task_notes` has ten columns: serial PK; required paper/creator/title/plain content; nullable task/deletion timestamp; positive integer version default 1; timezone-aware creation/update defaults. It has both proposed indexes and the restrictive composite `(task_id,paper_id)` task reference. All six FKs use RESTRICT deletion/NO ACTION update. Six CHECKs, two PKs, one UNIQUE and six FKs are represented; two sequences and three constraint-backing indexes arise from serial PKs/UNIQUE. The three explicit indexes bring the new index total to six.

The nullable task association can be explicitly unlinked while preserving required paper identity; a linked note must reference the same paper as its task. Task deletion cannot cascade into notes and remains restricted until C2's authorized transaction unlinks them. These are inspected SQL/schema guarantees, not executed PostgreSQL acceptance results.

### Conflicts and drafts

- A conflict keeps unsaved text/task selection and disables further saves. The UI explains that the note changed and offers Reload latest version. Reload requires explicit confirmation that it replaces the draft, reads the authorized current note, then resets only that dialog to the returned version. It never automatically retries a mutation or merges drafts. A failed latest read preserves the original draft; changed deletion/restoration state keeps the write blocked and instructs a workspace reload.
- Existing ResearchDialog protects dirty close/Cancel/Escape and document unload. The project selector and tabs are disabled while a form is open or work is pending; uncertain writes/refresh failures pause further changes until workspace verification. Failed validation/denial/uncertain saves do not reset the form; synchronous submission locks prevent accidental duplicate actions. No global/persistent draft store.
- A feature-detected Navigation API navigate listener also guards cancelable same-document history navigation. Its cancellation branch was tested with a synthetic cancelable event, not real Next.js history. Browsers without that API, noncancelable history events and browser/OS termination may still discard an in-memory draft without that extra history prompt. Ordinary project/tab changes remain locked until dialog dismissal; broader history/device behavior belongs in combined acceptance.
